meta.tagline: The city where East and West shake hands in a bazaar

pills: A civilization in a cup of Bosnian coffee

overview.title: Welcome to Sarajevo
overview.intro: In Sarajevo you change centuries on a single street: the Austro-Hungarian facades of Ferhadija end at one point, and the cobbles of the Ottoman bazaar begin — the 'Sarajevo Meeting of Cultures' marker on the pavement is no joke. In Baščaršija the coppersmiths' hammers ring, and four faiths face one square: mosque, cathedral, church and synagogue all within a short walk. This city has seen a siege and an Olympics; it doesn't hide its scars, yet it greets you with hospitality at its warmest. The coffee cup is small and the conversation long — Sarajevo is no city for the hurried.

local_word.definition: A word that came into Bosnian from the Turkish 'keyif' and deepened along the way: the pleasure of doing something exactly your own way, without hurry. Sipping Bosnian coffee from a fildžan, wandering the bazaar with no aim — all of it is ćejf. For a Sarajevan, ćejf is non-negotiable: once they say 'ćejf mi je', the matter is closed.

rules.title: Drink coffee the Bosnian way, and never rush it
rules.description: Bosnian coffee is not espresso: it arrives in a copper džezva, is poured slowly into a tiny fildžan cup, with Turkish delight and sugar alongside. Don't drop the sugar in — bite a corner and sip. A coffee that takes less than half an hour doesn't count as coffee.

rules.title: Walk both faces of the city
rules.description: Don't stay only in Baščaršija: the Habsburg facades of Ferhadija, the story of the Latin Bridge and the socialist-era blocks are layers of this city too. Give an afternoon to the 'century walk' — from the Ottomans to Austria to today, all on one street.

rules.title: Approach the war's memory with respect
rules.description: The red resin marks in the pavement — the Sarajevo Roses — are mortar shell craters; not stepping on them is a courtesy. Visit the Tunnel Museum and the Srebrenica gallery, but keep photos and questions measured: here the war is lived memory, not tourist scenery.

tip.label: The Sarajevo philosophy
tip.text: In this city plans aren't made, they're brewed: the morning coffee stretches, a bazaar conversation interrupts, and in the evening the call to prayer and church bells rise together over Žuta Tabija. Follow your ćejf, not your watch.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The historic center is walkable; the tram runs the length of the valley, and the Trebević cable car serves the city from above.

items.title: Arriving from the airport
items.description: Sarajevo Airport is 25 minutes from the center: take a taxi but fix the price before you get in, or ask your hotel for a transfer. Direct flights arrive daily from many European cities — one of the Balkans' best weekend-escape airports.

items.title: The tram line
items.description: One of Europe's oldest tram lines runs east-west along the valley: a single line covers Baščaršija to Ilidža. Buy your ticket at a kiosk and validate it on board — checks are rare, but it's the custom.

items.title: A walkable center
items.description: Baščaršija, Ferhadija, the Latin Bridge and the cathedral are steps apart: the historic core can be walked in half a day. Comfortable shoes for the cobblestones — bazaar breaks stretch the walk sweetly.

items.title: The Trebević cable car
items.description: Rising from just above Baščaršija, the cable car reaches the Trebević ridges in nine minutes: the city at your feet, pine resin in the air. The abandoned Olympic bobsled track up top is now a walking route.

items.title: Taxis and day tours
items.description: Taxis are cheap, but have the meter turned on — thank the ones who refuse and move on. For the Tunnel Museum, Vrelo Bosne and the mountain villages, day tours or a pre-agreed taxi are the practical answer.

callout.label: Cable car tip
callout.text: Ride up Trebević in the late afternoon: you see the city first in daylight, then at the hour of the evening call to prayer on the way down. Walk the bobsled track, take a coffee at the ridge cafe — the sunset from the descending cabin is Sarajevo's best view 'ticket'.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Sarajevo, choosing a base means choosing a layer: inside the Ottoman bazaar, along the Habsburg boulevards, or up in the view-blessed hill quarters.

local_word.definition: The Bosnian sibling of the Turkish 'mahalle' — neighborhood: the old Sarajevo fabric climbing the hills with its mosques, fountains and gardens. In mahalas like Vratnik and Bjelave, life still runs at neighborly scale — bakery scents in the morning, window conversations at night.

items.name: Around Baščaršija
items.description: Guesthouses and boutique hotels beside the bazaar's stone lanes: you wake to the coppersmith's hammer and walk to the bazaar grills at night. Central and atmospheric — lively on summer evenings.

items.name: Ferhadija and the center
items.description: Hotels in Habsburg-faced buildings: the pedestrian street, the cathedral and the bazaar at hand. A practical base at the exact midpoint of two centuries, walking distance to everything.

items.name: Bjelave
items.description: A quiet mahala ten uphill minutes from the center: apartments and guest houses, gardened homes, bakery and greengrocer life. For those who want Sarajevo's everyday face.

items.name: Vratnik
items.description: The quarter of the old fortress gates: from guesthouses beside Žuta Tabija the city lies at your feet. It demands a climb, but you watch the sunset from your balcony.

items.name: Novo Sarajevo and Grbavica
items.description: Modern apartments along the tram line: soft prices, ten minutes to the center by tram. A practical zone that eases the budget on longer stays.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Sarajevo tells a different story each season: summer is festive, winter is snowy with Olympic spirit; spring and autumn are walking's golden setting.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Valley Wakes
items.subtitle: Spring · Greening hills, cool bazaar mornings
items.description: The Miljacka valley turns green, coffee gardens spill onto the streets, and the springs of Vrelo Bosne run at their fullest. The weather is made for walking and the crowds are thin — the season for peeling back the city's layers in peace.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May the Trebević slopes bloom: ride the cable car up, walk along the bobsled track, and come down for the first open-air coffee of the year in the bazaar. Mountain and bazaar in one day — Sarajevo's classic double.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Festival Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Film festival, full coffee gardens
items.description: In August the Sarajevo Film Festival rolls out the red carpet: squares become open-air cinemas and bazaar nights run long. Days are warm but mountain coolness is near — the evenings are always fresh.

callout.label: Festival note
callout.text: In festival week, rooms sell out months ahead and prices multiply: book early if your dates align. If you'd rather avoid it, skip mid-August — same summer, half the price.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Chestnuts and Mist
items.subtitle: Autumn · Golden hills, smoky valleys
items.description: The hills turn gold, roast chestnut smoke rises in the bazaar, and morning mist wraps the minaret tips. The crowds recede and coffee conversations move indoors — the season of photographers and slow travelers.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: On an October morning, climb to Žuta Tabija: the valley lies under the mist, the minarets above it — Sarajevo's most legendary frame is shot at this hour. On the way down, it's exactly time for a hot burek.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Olympic White
items.subtitle: Winter · Snowy bazaar, ski mountains at the door
items.description: When snow falls, Baščaršija becomes a postcard: copper domes whiten, coffee steam curls. The mountains of the 1984 Olympics — Jahorina and Bjelašnica — offer skiing half an hour away: the city-plus-slopes double is among Europe's most affordable.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: Skiing on Jahorina in the morning, ćevapi and hot salep in the bazaar at night: that's the double menu of a Sarajevo winter. Lift passes cost a quarter of the Alps — and renting gear is easy and cheap.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Bosnian cooking is the Ottoman table steeped in mountain air: grill smoke, buttery pastry and coffee drunk slowly.

local_word.definition: Small grilled meat fingers tucked into somun flatbread: Sarajevo's national dish. Raw onion and kajmak cream on the side, drinking yoghurt to wash it down — the garnish debate is closed. The answer to 'how many?' is five or ten; the master knows the count, you know your appetite.

items.name: Ćevapi
items.description: Finger-sized kebabs off the coals, inside wood-oven somun bread: kajmak and onion rings alongside. Eaten in the bazaar's ćevabdžinicas — don't look for ketchup; this table's rule is simplicity.

items.name: Burek and the pita family
items.description: Spinning trays at the buregdžinica counter: meat burek, cheese sirnica, spinach zeljanica, potato krompiruša. Sold by weight, doused with yoghurt — the morning tray is the freshest.
items.tag: By weight off the tray · with yoghurt

items.name: Begova čorba and klepe
items.description: The chicken-and-okra 'bey's soup' is Ottoman heritage by the spoonful; klepe are Bosnian dumplings under garlic yoghurt. Both are everyday fare at an aščinica, the home-cooking eatery.

items.name: The Bosnian coffee ritual
items.description: It arrives foaming in a copper džezva: fildžan cup, lokum, a glass of water. Leave the grounds at the bottom, stretch the conversation — in Sarajevo coffee is not a drink but a unit of appointment.

items.name: Tufahija and hurmašica
items.description: Tufahija, a walnut-stuffed apple in syrup, and hurmašica, syrup-soaked semolina fingers: take them with coffee at a bazaar sweet shop. The syrup is serious, the portions friendly — sharing is allowed.

items.name: Somun and kajmak breakfast
items.description: Hot somun from the wood oven, spread with fresh kajmak and honey: the plain mountain breakfast. If there's a queue outside the bakery on Sunday morning, you're in the right place — the scent of hot somun gives directions.
items.tag: Hot from the oven · mountain style

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: In Sarajevo, a good eatery's fame lies in the shortness of its menu: a ćevabdžinica makes only ćevapi, a buregdžinica only pastry — that's how mastery works. If you can't decide, follow the locals' queue at noon and the smell of the grill at night.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees Baščaršija and the Latin Bridge; these six are the hidden pages that open the city's layers.

items.name: Žuta Tabija (Yellow Fortress)
items.description: From Vratnik's old bastion the whole valley lies at your feet: locals arrive at dusk with thermoses, and the call to prayer echoes across the hills. In Ramadan the iftar cannon fires from here — and every evening of the year the sunset is a free performance.

items.name: The Trebević bobsled track
items.description: The 1984 Olympic bobsled run curls through the pine forest like a graffiti-covered concrete river: you walk inside it, and the photos are legendary. Ride the cable car up and descend on foot along the track.

items.name: The Tunnel of Hope (Tunel spasa)
items.description: The museum of the 800-meter tunnel dug under the airport runway during the siege, entered through a family house: the city's lifeline for four years. A heavy visit, but the key to understanding Sarajevo.

items.name: Svrzo House
items.description: An 18th-century Bosnian mansion: the selamlik-haremlik layout, divan-lined rooms and a courtyard, kept as a museum-house. Ten minutes above Baščaršija, a time capsule the crowds never reach.

items.name: Inat Kuća (House of Spite)
items.description: The house of the man who, refusing to yield to the Austrian city hall project, had his home moved stone by stone across the river: today a traditional restaurant. The story outdelivers the menu — 'inat' means stubborn pride here too.

items.rarity: Spring park at the city's edge
items.name: Vrelo Bosne
items.description: The park where the Bosna River is born: swan ponds, giant plane trees and the carriage-lined avenue from Ilidža. An afternoon escape from the tram's last stop — the place where the city breathes.

callout.label: Layer strategy
callout.text: Tour Sarajevo layer by layer: Ottoman in the morning (bazaar + mahala), Habsburg at noon (Ferhadija + cathedral), the 20th century in the afternoon (tunnel + bobsled track), and the view of them all at dusk (Žuta Tabija). Four layers, one city — breaking the order is allowed.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Sarajevo is an honest city, but a tourist's inexperience invites the same games everywhere; know these four.

items.name: The meterless taxi
items.description: On airport runs and late-night rides some drivers quote a 'fixed price' instead of the meter; the number is often two or three times reality.
items.instead: Ask for the meter before getting in; thank those who refuse and take the next cab. App-based rides or a hotel transfer are the cleanest solution. City distances are short anyway.

items.name: Euro payments, creative rounding
items.description: Some tourist spots accept euros but set their own exchange rate and give change in KM: a few euros evaporate each time.
items.instead: Pay in KM: the rate is fixed (1 EUR ≈ 1.95 KM) and ATMs are everywhere. Keep small KM notes for bazaar stalls that don't take cards.

items.name: Mass-produced 'handmade' copper
items.description: At some bazaar stalls, machine-pressed džezvas and trays are sold with a hand-hammered story; the shiny display often hides imports.
items.instead: Buy from a workshop on Kazandžiluk lane where you hear the hammer: the master shows his work and engraves your name. Pens made from bullet casings are an authentic Sarajevo keepsake too — hear their story from the maker.

items.name: War tours turned into a show
items.description: Some 'war tours' turn the siege into sensational scenery: speed, poses and dramatic music — respect for lived experience falls behind.
items.instead: Visit the Tunnel Museum, the Siege Museum and Galerija 11/07/95 at your own pace, or choose a small group with a local guide. Ask questions, don't pose — memory is taken seriously in this city.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Sarajevo the measure is sincerity: keep the haggling short and the smiling generous. A shopkeeper's offer of coffee is not a trap but a gift — sit, drink, talk. The most precious thing in this city is free: people's time.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From bazaar to bastion — a day of layers

steps.title: Buregdžinica breakfast
steps.description: Burek off the morning tray, yoghurt on top: start the day the Bosnian way. The scent of hot somun from the bakery next door — don't resist.

steps.title: Baščaršija and Kazandžiluk
steps.description: Pigeons at the Sebilj fountain, hammer song on the coppersmiths' lane, the Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque and the bedesten: the Ottoman layer, best in morning calm.

steps.title: The century walk
steps.description: Walk Ferhadija east to west: stop at the 'Meeting of Cultures' line on the pavement, then take a coffee break on the cathedral square.

steps.title: Ćevapi noon
steps.description: Five ćevapi with kajmak and onion at a bazaar ćevabdžinica: drinking yoghurt alongside. Simple, smoky, beyond debate.

steps.title: Latin Bridge and museums
steps.description: Stand at Franz Ferdinand's corner where world history turned; then the Siege Museum or Svrzo House — whichever century you choose.

steps.title: Žuta Tabija sunset
steps.description: Climb through Vratnik to the bastion: the valley turns crimson, the call to prayer and church bells mingle. On the way down, tufahija and one last coffee in the bazaar — a fildžan ends slowly.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Bazaar, memory and mountain — the full Sarajevo

steps.title: Classic Sarajevo
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: burek, Baščaršija, the century walk, ćevapi, the Latin Bridge, Žuta Tabija.

steps.title: Memory and heights
steps.description: Morning at the Tunnel of Hope and Galerija 11/07/95; begova čorba and klepe at an aščinica for lunch; cable car up Trebević in the afternoon — bobsled track walk; a quiet mahala restaurant in Bjelave for dinner.

steps.title: Springs and farewell
steps.description: Tram to Ilidža in the morning, then walk or take a carriage down the plane-tree avenue to the Vrelo Bosne springs; trout by the water for lunch; on the return, a džezva-fildžan set and a packet of coffee from the bazaar — drink your farewell cup in the Morića Han courtyard.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Bosnian will sound familiar to Turkish ears — hundreds of shared words; with these five, the doors open for you too.

items.meaning: Yes — 'merhaba' works in Bosnian too! Greet the bazaar this way; a smile is guaranteed
Thank you — when the coffee cup empties, and at every act of hospitality
Please / you're welcome / pardon — Bosnian's multi-purpose key of courtesy
Enjoy your meal — said to anyone sitting down; you'll hear it over ćevapi
Cheers! — as glasses rise; the reply is eye contact and a smile

checklist.title: Sarajevo Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Ćejf complete! You've lived the city of East and West the way it deserves!
